description.narrative: The development objective of the Human Capital Program for Georgia is to make the human capital delivery system in Georgia more efficient and inclusive. The Government of Georgia (GoG) program for human capital for 2022-2031 provides a set of transformative policy priorities for the development of human capital and its effective engagement in the development of the country. The portion of the GoG program for human capital for 2022-2031 that will be implemented in the period 2022-2027 under this operation is termed as the GoG Program for human capital for 2022-2027, and forms the Program Boundary. The Program is composed of a set of subprograms that have been organized in three results areas: efficiency for better value for money of human capital expenditures in education, health and social protection sectors. Inclusion for quality of human capital expenditures for all beneficiaries in education, health and social protection sectors. Connectivity of digital systems across all areas of human capital provision in education, health and social protection sectors.
To make the human capital delivery system in Georgia more efficient and inclusive.

condition.narrative: Schedule II, Section I (A) 2. The Borrower shall, no later than 120 days after the Effective Date, unless agreed otherwise betweenthe Bank and the Borrower, establish and thereafter maintain throughout the implementation of the Program, a ministerial-levelcommittee (“Human Capital Steering Committee” or “HCSC”), chaired by MOF, with representatives from MOES, MOILHSA, and otherrelevant ministries and entities, to oversee the overall coordination of Program implementation, with staffing and resourcesappropriate to fulfil its functions under the Program.

Schedule II, Section I (A) 3. The Borrower shall, no later than 120 days after the Effective Date, unless agreed otherwise betweenthe Bank and the Borrower, establish and thereafter maintain, throughout the implementation of the Program, a unit (“ProgramCoordination Unit” or “PCU”) to coordinate and monitor Program implementation (including implementation, monitoring, and reportingon environmental and social aspects), within the MOF, consisting of members from the MOF, MOES, and MOILHSA, with staffing andresources appropriate to fulfil its functions under the Program.

Schedule II, Section I (A) 4. The Borrower shall, through MOES and MOILHSA, in collaboration with MOF, no later than 120 days afterthe Effective Date, unless agreed otherwise between the Bank and the Borrower, hire or appoint at least two environmental andsocial specialists to the PCU, with one specialist reporting to MOES and one specialist reporting to MOILHSA, under terms ofreference satisfactory to the Bank.

title.narrative: Reduction in the rural urban gap in UNE scores

comment.narrative: Target achieved. This indicator measures the reduction in rural-urban gap in Unified National Examinations (UNE) scores for foreign languages, science, and mathematics. Rural refers to 31 municipalities with 75% of more rural population and urban refers to 15 municipalities with 0% rural population (population data reported from 2021 Geostat). In February 2024, NAEC reported baseline (2019) absolute values were 43 and 30 for urban and rural areas (difference of 13 percentage points) (correction from previous value which was reported as 14 percentage points). Other updated values: 9 in 2020, 8 in 2021, 10 in 2022, 9 in 2023, 9 in 2024. Current value reported in this ISR refers to year 2024, absolute values were 37 and 28 for urban and rural areas. MOESY has presented a complementary methodology to measure the rural-urban gap in UNE scores after a new data sharing agreement between NAEC and EMIS has made possible the identification of rural status to individual level data.

title.narrative: Average number of outpatient consultations per person per annum at PHC providers

comment.narrative: Target achieved. The indicator shows the average number of per capita outpatient visits to the primary health care facilities of MoILHSA and private providers. Baseline value refers to year 2020 and current value reported in this ISR refers to updated data for the full year 2024. Data for 2025 will be available after May 2026.

title.narrative: Percentage of TSA benefits going to households in the poorest quintile

comment.narrative:
Underperforming and potentially in need of revision.
This indicator measures the share of targeted social assistance benefits (inclusive of child allowance) received by people in the bottom quintile of the population's consumption distribution over TSA total benefit expenditures.
The latest value (November 2025) refers to coverage during calendar year 2023 and is computed from the Household Income and Expenditure Survey.
The value indicates a worsening in the quality of poverty targeting, due to two factors: (1) the delays in the adoption of the new TSA scoring formula, which was expected in 2023; (2) the unforeseen expansion of child allowance delivered jointly with the TSA benefits and less poverty-targeted than the basic TSA.
While factor (1) is attributable to the program, factor (2) presents an issue of attributability of the indicator and may require a change in the measurement or the name of the indicator.

title.narrative: Percentage of newly listed on-patent medicines for which a managed entry agreement was signed in the past year

comment.narrative: Annual target achieved for calendar year 2023 but not achieved in 2024 although the MEA contract was signed on January 10, 2025. Based on the official request for approval of adjustments to the verification protocol and procedure for the related DLR (DLR 1.3), the National Health Agency expanded the scope of the Managed Entry Agreement (MEA) mechanism during 2023–2024 to include products covered by various state-funded healthcare programs, not just the Universal Health Care Program. The achievement for 2025 will be reported in first quarter of 2026.

title.narrative: Percentage of female enrollment in IT related courses under new Upper Secondary curriculum

comment.narrative: Delayed. As of October 20 2025, schools were not yet operating under the new fourth generation curriculum. The indicator measures the number of female students enrolled in IT related courses under the new curriculum over the total number of students enrolled in IT related courses under the new curriculum (all schools). 50.7% of female students are enrolled in IT related courses in upper secondary under the existing curriculum.

title.narrative: Number of schools that meet minimum quality standards

comment.narrative: On track. This indicator measures the number of schools covering grade 10 to 12 that are authorized and thus meet the minimum quality standards established under the authorization process by the MOES. 300 schools in 2023 and 79 schools in 2024 were authorized and complied with environmental and social policy. 80 schools in 2024 and 2025 were authorized and are in the undergoing environmental screening. The remaining schools are scheduled to be authorized and undertake screening in 2025 and 2026.

title.narrative: Percentage of annual out-of-pocket spending on health care that is allocated to medicines

comment.narrative: On track. This indicator measures the share of medical expenditures in households total out-of-pocket health expenditure. Baseline value refers to year 2020 and current value reported in this ISR are from MoILHSA System of Accounts data in 2024. The increase in out-of-pocket payments is attributable to a change in the methodology for calculating GDP. At the end of 2024, GDP values were updated in accordance with the System of Health Accounts 2008 methodology. GEOSTAT now utilizes supply-use tables for GDP estimation and applies the residual approach for final consumption. To estimate household spending on healthcare in Georgia (OOPs), GEOSTAT relies on the Household Income and Expenditure Survey (HIES) and relevant COICOP (Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose) categories. https://www.geostat.ge/ka/modules/categories/119/methodologia-erovnuli-angarishebi; https://www.geostat.ge/media/60239/GDP_Revision_12.10.2024.pdf The actual current figures are already reca

title.narrative: Adoption of gender responsive curricula in the new secondary education curriculum

comment.narrative: Delayed. A gender analysis of the third generation curriculum has been completed and its key findings indicate that the curriculum is not gender-sensitive. Consultations with gender specialists were carried out and a gender responsive curricula is being considered in the revision of the fourth generation curricula completed in 2025. However, the new curricula has not been implemented yet.

title.narrative: Share of vacancies filled through the Worknet job-matching portal

comment.narrative:
Delayed.
The Worknet job matching function is now expected to be launched in January 2026, and the indicator will be measured from that point onwards.
The indicator captures the percentage share of vacancies posted on Worknet in the reporting period that have been filled through recruitment of a Worknet-registered jobseeker (where the worknet-registered jobseeker was registered on Worknet before the date of posting of the vacancy), out of all vacancies posted in the same period. The denominator will include also vacancies that have subsequently been canceled, closed, and/or removed.

title.narrative: Percentage of university admissions coming from regions with rural population greater than 50%

comment.narrative: Target Exceeded. This indicator captured the share of persons enrolled in higher education from those regions where over 50% of the population resides in the countryside (includes all regions, except Tbilisi, Imereti and Adjara) of the total number of enrolled persons . In previous years, the Imereti region was included in the calculation because its rural population exceeded 50%. However, since the rural population in Imereti has now fallen below 50%, we no longer include the region in the calculation.
